references.text: Isaiah 59:21 promises that God's Spirit will be with the people and in their mouths, which directly foreshadows Jesus' promise that the Spirit of truth will be with the disciples and be in them.

Ezekiel 36:27 describes God's Spirit as dwelling within the people to give them the ability to follow God's commands, a parallel to the idea that the Spirit will be in the disciples and grant them recognition of the truth.
Jeremiah 31:33 speaks of God's law being written on the heart, which corresponds with the inner presence and knowledge of the Spirit described in John 14:17.
John 16:13 identifies the Spirit as the "Spirit of truth" who will guide the disciples into all truth, a direct continuation of the title and function given in 14:17.
John 15:26 refers to the "Spirit of Truth" who will testify about Jesus, linking the Spirit's identity to the truth about Christ, which is central in 14:17.

1 John 2:20 confirms that believers have received an anointing from the Holy One and know the truth, echoing the contrast between the world's lack of understanding and the disciples' knowledge found in 14:17.
